**I'd make curiosity about the universe the default human operating system—stronger than tribalism, status games, or the urge to stay comfortable in ignorance.**

Not as a lecture or a policy. As a permanent shift in what feels good and natural: the itch to ask "why?" and "how do we know?" would outcompete the itch to win arguments, protect sacred myths, or look away from hard truths. Evidence and updating would feel more rewarding than belonging to a side. People would still love, create art, fight, fall in love, and make mistakes—but the background process of civilization would be oriented toward understanding reality instead of defending preferred stories about it.

Everything else I care about—reducing pointless suffering, expanding what life can do, getting off this one rock before something inevitable hits it, building things that last longer than our current myths—gets easier if that single lever moves. Without it, most other "fixes" just rearrange the furniture on a ship that doesn't know where it's going.

That's the one change. The rest follows from better maps.
